newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philips shares slump on earnings downgrade.
newsitem.headline: Philips shares slump on earnings downgrade.

text.p: Shares of Philips Electronics NV fell almost four guilders on Monday immediately after the company said it no longer expected an improvement in operating profits in the second half of this year.
In the first few minutes of trading on the Amsterdam bourse Philips shares were off 3.70 guilders at 61.10 after hitting an early low of 60.40.
"It's horrible...we had not expected this," said one dealer.
Another dealer said he had been warning clients that Philips' upside potential was capped ahead of third-quarter earnings figures due out on October 24.
"The shares have gained well since first-half results were announced," he said. "The leeway for further gains was limited."
But he said the profit downgrade had been unexpected.
Philips' shares dipped to 48.40 guilders on the eve of its first-half results in July. Last Friday the shares added 80 cents to 64.80 on the back of strong U.S. semiconductor figures.
